# Question 1: Locking the Tree of Space
# You have a world map represented as an M-Ary tree (sample tree below):

# You need to define three operations on it:
# lock(X, uid)
# unlock(X, uid)
# upgradeLock(X, uid)
# Where X is the name of a node in the tree (which is unique), and uid is the user performing the operation.
# Definitions for the Operations:
# Lock(X, uid):
# Lock takes exclusive access on the subtree rooted at X. Once lock(X, uid) succeeds:
# lock(A, anyUserId) should fail (returns false), where A is a descendant of X.
# lock(B, anyUserId) should fail (returns false), where X is a descendant of B.
# Lock operation cannot be performed on a node that is already locked, i.e., lock(X, anyUserId) should fail (returns false).
# Unlock(X, uid):
# Unlock reverts what was done by the lock operation. It can only be called on the same node on which user uid had called a lock before. Returns true if successful.
# UpgradeLock(X, uid):
# This helps the user uid upgrade their lock to an ancestor node. It is only possible if the node X already has locked descendants and all of them are locked by the same user uid. Upgrade should fail if there is any node which is a descendant of X that is locked by a different user. A successful upgrade will "lock" the node. UpgradeLock must not violate the consistency model required by Lock/Unlock.
# Notes:
# The number of nodes in the tree, N, is very large, so optimize the time complexity for the above algorithms.
# Input Format:
# The first line contains the number of nodes in the tree (N).
# The second line contains the number of children per node (m in an m-ary tree).
# The third line contains the number of queries (Q).
# Next N lines contain the NodeName (string) in the m-Ary Tree.
# The next Q lines contain queries in the format: OperationType NodeName UserId.
# Operation Type:
# 1 for Lock
# 2 for Unlock
# 3 for UpgradeLock
# NodeName: The name of any node (unique) in the m-Ary Tree.
# UserId: An integer representing a unique user.
# Example Input:
# 7
# 2
# 3
# World
# Asia
# Africa
# China
# India
# South Africa
# Egypt
# 1 China 9
# 2 India 9
# 3 Asia 9


# This input represents a 2-ary tree with 7 nodes as follows:
#            World
#            /     \
#       Asia        Africa
#      /    \       /     \
#  China  India  South Africa  Egypt


# Additional Notes:
# The tree is always fully balanced.
# Constraints:
# (1 < N < 5 \times 10^5)
# (1 < m < 30)
# (1 < Q < 5 \times 10^5)
# (1 < \text{length of NodeName} < 20)
# Optimize the time complexity:
# Lock: (O(\log_m N))
# Unlock: (O(\log_m N))
# UpgradeLock: (O(\text{numberOfLockedNodes} \times \log_m N))
# The lock operation on an already locked node should fail.
# Once UpgradeLock(X, uid) succeeds on X, it is equivalent to X being locked by uid. As per the definition, Lock(A/B, anyUser) should fail, and Unlock(X, uid) should also work.
# Upgrade lock operation on a node having no locked descendants should fail, and upgrade lock on an already locked node should also fail.


import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, val):
        self.val = val          # Node value (name)
        self.uid = None         # User ID who locked the node
        self.parent = None      # Reference to parent node
        self.children = []      # List of child nodes
        self.isLocked = False   # Lock status
        self.lockedDescendantCount = 0  # Number of locked descendants


class Tree:
    def __init__(self, n, m, node_list, queries):
        self.node_list = []
        self.node_map = {}

        # Create node instances and map node names to instances
        for name in node_list:
            node = Node(name)
            self.node_list.append(node)
            self.node_map[name] = node

        # Assign children to each node based on m-ary tree properties
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(m):
                child_index = m * i + j + 1
                if child_index < n:
                    self.node_list[i].children.append(self.node_list[child_index])
                    self.node_list[child_index].parent = self.node_list[i]

        self.root = self.node_list[0]

        # Process queries
        self.processed_queries = [query.strip().split() for query in queries]

    def lock(self, node, uid):
        # Check if node is already locked
        if node.isLocked:
            return False

        # Check if any ancestors are locked
        if self.isAncestorLocked(node):
            return False

        # Check if any descendants are locked
        if node.lockedDescendantCount > 0:
            return False

        # Lock the node
        node.isLocked = True
        node.uid = uid

        # Update ancestors' lockedDescendantCount
        parent = node.parent
        while parent:
            parent.lockedDescendantCount += 1
            parent = parent.parent

        return True

    def unlock(self, node, uid):
        # Check if node is locked by uid
        if not node.isLocked or node.uid != uid:
            return False

        # Unlock the node
        node.isLocked = False
        node.uid = None

        # Update ancestors' lockedDescendantCount
        parent = node.parent
        while parent:
            parent.lockedDescendantCount -= 1
            parent = parent.parent

        return True

    def upgrade(self, node, uid):
        # Check if node is already locked
        if node.isLocked:
            return False

        # Check if any ancestors are locked
        if self.isAncestorLocked(node):
            return False

        # Check if there are any locked descendants
        if node.lockedDescendantCount == 0:
            return False  # No locked descendants to upgrade

        # Collect all locked descendants
        locked_descendants = []
        if not self.collectLockedDescendants(node, uid, locked_descendants):
            return False  # Cannot upgrade due to locks by other users

        # Unlock all locked descendants
        for descendant in locked_descendants:
            descendant.isLocked = False
            descendant.uid = None
            # Update ancestors' lockedDescendantCount
            parent = descendant.parent
            while parent:
                parent.lockedDescendantCount -= 1
                parent = parent.parent

        # Lock the node
        node.isLocked = True
        node.uid = uid

        # Update ancestors' lockedDescendantCount
        parent = node.parent
        while parent:
            parent.lockedDescendantCount += 1
            parent = parent.parent

        return True

    def isAncestorLocked(self, node):
        # Traverse up to check if any ancestor is locked
        current = node.parent
        while current:
            if current.isLocked:
                return True
            current = current.parent
        return False

    def collectLockedDescendants(self, node, uid, locked_nodes):
        # If there are no locked descendants, return True
        if node.lockedDescendantCount == 0:
            return True

        # Check if current node is locked
        if node.isLocked:
            if node.uid == uid:
                locked_nodes.append(node)
            else:
                # Locked by a different user
                return False

        # Recurse into children only if necessary
        for child in node.children:
            if child.lockedDescendantCount > 0:
                if not self.collectLockedDescendants(child, uid, locked_nodes):
                    return False
        return True

    def process_queries(self):
        results = []
        for query in self.processed_queries:
            operation, node_name, uid = query
            node = self.node_map[node_name]
            if operation == "1":
                result = self.lock(node, uid)
            elif operation == "2":
                result = self.unlock(node, uid)
            elif operation == "3":
                result = self.upgrade(node, uid)
            else:
                result = False  # Invalid operation
            results.append('true' if result else 'false')
        return results


def main():
    n = int(sys.stdin.readline())
    m = int(sys.stdin.readline())
    q = int(sys.stdin.readline())

    node_list = []
    for _ in range(n):
        node_list.append(sys.stdin.readline().strip())

    queries = []
    for _ in range(q):
        queries.append(sys.stdin.readline().strip())

    tree = Tree(n, m, node_list, queries)
    results = tree.process_queries()
    for res in results:
        print(res)

main()

# Question 1: Locking the Tree of Space
# You have a world map represented as an M-Ary tree (sample tree below):

# You need to define three operations on it:
# lock(X, uid)
# unlock(X, uid)
# upgradeLock(X, uid)
# Where X is the name of a node in the tree (which is unique), and uid is the user performing the operation.
# Definitions for the Operations:
# Lock(X, uid):
# Lock takes exclusive access on the subtree rooted at X. Once lock(X, uid) succeeds:
# lock(A, anyUserId) should fail (returns false), where A is a descendant of X.
# lock(B, anyUserId) should fail (returns false), where X is a descendant of B.
# Lock operation cannot be performed on a node that is already locked, i.e., lock(X, anyUserId) should fail (returns false).
# Unlock(X, uid):
# Unlock reverts what was done by the lock operation. It can only be called on the same node on which user uid had called a lock before. Returns true if successful.
# UpgradeLock(X, uid):
# This helps the user uid upgrade their lock to an ancestor node. It is only possible if the node X already has locked descendants and all of them are locked by the same user uid. Upgrade should fail if there is any node which is a descendant of X that is locked by a different user. A successful upgrade will "lock" the node. UpgradeLock must not violate the consistency model required by Lock/Unlock.
# Notes:
# The number of nodes in the tree, N, is very large, so optimize the time complexity for the above algorithms.
# Input Format:
# The first line contains the number of nodes in the tree (N).
# The second line contains the number of children per node (m in an m-ary tree).
# The third line contains the number of queries (Q).
# Next N lines contain the NodeName (string) in the m-Ary Tree.
# The next Q lines contain queries in the format: OperationType NodeName UserId.
# Operation Type:
# 1 for Lock
# 2 for Unlock
# 3 for UpgradeLock
# NodeName: The name of any node (unique) in the m-Ary Tree.
# UserId: An integer representing a unique user.
# Example Input:
# 7
# 2
# 3
# World
# Asia
# Africa
# China
# India
# South Africa
# Egypt
# 1 China 9
# 2 India 9
# 3 Asia 9


# This input represents a 2-ary tree with 7 nodes as follows:
#            World
#            /     \
#       Asia        Africa
#      /    \       /     \
#  China  India  South Africa  Egypt


# Additional Notes:
# The tree is always fully balanced.
# Constraints:
# (1 < N < 5 \times 10^5)
# (1 < m < 30)
# (1 < Q < 5 \times 10^5)
# (1 < \text{length of NodeName} < 20)
# Optimize the time complexity:
# Lock: (O(\log_m N))
# Unlock: (O(\log_m N))
# UpgradeLock: (O(\text{numberOfLockedNodes} \times \log_m N))
# The lock operation on an already locked node should fail.
# Once UpgradeLock(X, uid) succeeds on X, it is equivalent to X being locked by uid. As per the definition, Lock(A/B, anyUser) should fail, and Unlock(X, uid) should also work.
# Upgrade lock operation on a node having no locked descendants should fail, and upgrade lock on an already locked node should also fail.


import sys


class Node:
    def __init__(self, val):
        self.val = val          # Node value (name)
        self.uid = None         # User ID who locked the node
        self.parent = None      # Reference to parent node
        self.children = []      # List of child nodes
        self.isLocked = False   # Lock status
        self.lockedDescendantCount = 0  # Number of locked descendants


class Tree:
    def __init__(self, n, m, node_list, queries):
        self.node_list = []
        self.node_map = {}

        # Create node instances and map node names to instances
        for name in node_list:
            node = Node(name)
            self.node_list.append(node)
            self.node_map[name] = node

        # Assign children to each node based on m-ary tree properties
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(m):
                child_index = m * i + j + 1
                if child_index < n:
                    self.node_list[i].children.append(self.node_list[child_index])
                    self.node_list[child_index].parent = self.node_list[i]

        self.root = self.node_list[0]

        # Process queries
        self.processed_queries = [query.strip().split() for query in queries]

    def lock(self, node, uid):
        # Check if node is already locked
        if node.isLocked:
            return False

        # Check if any ancestors are locked
        if self.isAncestorLocked(node):
            return False

        # Check if any descendants are locked
        if node.lockedDescendantCount > 0:
            return False

        # Lock the node
        node.isLocked = True
        node.uid = uid

        # Update ancestors' lockedDescendantCount
        parent = node.parent
        while parent:
            parent.lockedDescendantCount += 1
            parent = parent.parent

        return True

    def unlock(self, node, uid):
        # Check if node is locked by uid
        if not node.isLocked or node.uid != uid:
            return False

        # Unlock the node
        node.isLocked = False
        node.uid = None

        # Update ancestors' lockedDescendantCount
        parent = node.parent
        while parent:
            parent.lockedDescendantCount -= 1
            parent = parent.parent

        return True

    def upgrade(self, node, uid):
        # Check if node is already locked
        if node.isLocked:
            return False

        # Check if any ancestors are locked
        if self.isAncestorLocked(node):
            return False

        # Check if there are any locked descendants
        if node.lockedDescendantCount == 0:
            return False  # No locked descendants to upgrade

        # Collect all locked descendants
        locked_descendants = []
        if not self.collectLockedDescendants(node, uid, locked_descendants):
            return False  # Cannot upgrade due to locks by other users

        # Unlock all locked descendants
        for descendant in locked_descendants:
            descendant.isLocked = False
            descendant.uid = None
            # Update ancestors' lockedDescendantCount
            parent = descendant.parent
            while parent:
                parent.lockedDescendantCount -= 1
                parent = parent.parent

        # Lock the node
        node.isLocked = True
        node.uid = uid

        # Update ancestors' lockedDescendantCount
        parent = node.parent
        while parent:
            parent.lockedDescendantCount += 1
            parent = parent.parent

        return True

    def isAncestorLocked(self, node):
        # Traverse up to check if any ancestor is locked
        current = node.parent
        while current:
            if current.isLocked:
                return True
            current = current.parent
        return False

    def collectLockedDescendants(self, node, uid, locked_nodes):
        # If there are no locked descendants, return True
        if node.lockedDescendantCount == 0:
            return True

        # Check if current node is locked
        if node.isLocked:
            if node.uid == uid:
                locked_nodes.append(node)
            else:
                # Locked by a different user
                return False

        # Recurse into children only if necessary
        for child in node.children:
            if child.lockedDescendantCount > 0:
                if not self.collectLockedDescendants(child, uid, locked_nodes):
                    return False
        return True

    def process_queries(self):
        results = []
        for query in self.processed_queries:
            operation, node_name, uid = query
            node = self.node_map[node_name]
            if operation == "1":
                result = self.lock(node, uid)
            elif operation == "2":
                result = self.unlock(node, uid)
            elif operation == "3":
                result = self.upgrade(node, uid)
            else:
                result = False  # Invalid operation
            results.append('true' if result else 'false')
        return results


def main():
    n = int(sys.stdin.readline())
    m = int(sys.stdin.readline())
    q = int(sys.stdin.readline())

    node_list = []
    for _ in range(n):
        node_list.append(sys.stdin.readline().strip())

    queries = []
    for _ in range(q):
        queries.append(sys.stdin.readline().strip())

    tree = Tree(n, m, node_list, queries)
    results = tree.process_queries()
    for res in results:
        print(res)

main()

In graph theory, an m-ary tree (for nonnegative integers m) (also known as n-ary, k-ary or k-way tree) is an arborescence (or an ordered tree) in which each node has no more than m children. A binary tree is the special case where m = 2, and a ternary tree is another case with m = 3 that limits its children to three. In graph theory, an arborescence is a directed graph in which, for a vertex u (called the root) and any other vertex v, there is exactly one directed path from u to v. A graph is a collection of vertices (also known as nodes) and edges that connect these vertices. A tree is a special type of graph that is connected and acyclic, meaning that there are no cycles in the graph. In a tree, there is a unique path between any two vertices, and there is a single vertex called the root that is used as the starting point for traversing the tree.

The selected materials should meet the following criteria:
Thermal Efficiency: Provide superior indoor cooling by repelling heat from the outside and allowing heat transfer from the interior to the exterior.
Lightweight: The materials should be lightweight to enable ease of transportation, especially in remote or rural areas of Ghana.
Fast Construction: The materials should contribute to a significant reduction in construction time, allowing for faster build cycles in a prefabricated, modular environment.
Structural Strength: The materials should be equal to or stronger than traditional methods in terms of durability and resilience, able to withstand environmental factors such as high heat, humidity, and potential seismic activity.
3. Layering and Assembly:
Explore the best layering technique to achieve the thermal properties mentioned. Consider how the combination of aerated concrete slabs, manufactured wood, mesh, and steel could be layered to achieve a heat-repelling exterior while allowing heat transfer from the interior.

Suggest methods to further reduce costs by optimizing sourcing, production, and transportation.
The cost of the final product should be reduced by at least 40% compared to traditional building methods.
6. Sustainability:
Consider the environmental impact of the selected materials. Ideally, they should be sourced sustainably and have a reduced carbon footprint compared to traditional construction methods.
Investigate the recyclability or reusability of the materials.
7. Testing and Validation:
Propose strategies for testing the viability and performance of the materials. This could include thermal efficiency tests, strength tests, and accelerated aging tests to determine the long-term durability.
Suggest any prototype development processes that could validate the performance of these materials in real-world conditions.
8. Scalability and Local Production:
Research whether these materials can be produced locally in Ghana, or if they can be sourced from nearby African countries at competitive prices.
Identify any logistical or supply chain challenges that might arise in sourcing or producing these materials locally.
Outcome Expectations:
Provide a detailed material recommendation that meets the outlined goals, including the best combination of materials, optimal layering techniques, bonding methods, and strategies for testing and scaling.

Step Into the Employer’s Shoes
Chess grandmasters step into their opponents’ shoes, trying to anticipate every move… Expert salespeople step into their prospects’ shoes, trying to understand their pains and desires… And we use this same tactic to write the perfect data scientist resume.

Here’s the thought experiment:

If you were the employer, what would you be looking for in a candidate?

Now, if the answer to that question sounds easy, you’re probably not thinking carefully enough. For example, “smart programmer with data and machine learning skills” is not detailed enough.

Instead, pretend you need to write a complete job description… How exactly would a data scientist help your business? Where would they fit in? Who would they work with/under? Which skills would you require? Which experiences would impress you?

Answering these questions will help you shape a coherent strategy right from the start.

To-Do List:

Carefully read the job descriptions for 5 positions you like.
Note the patterns. Which skills and experiences show up repeatedly?
Note the people. Will you work with the engineering team or with the analysts?
Write one or two paragraphs summarizing the perfect candidate in your own words.
Re-read this description each time you sit down to write or edit your resume! This will put you in the right frame of mind.

As per the perpetual inventory system, accounting entry is done for every stock transaction. Otherwise, it's done in larger intervals for example monthly or quarterly. Each warehouse is linked with a corresponding account head.

On receipt of items in a particular warehouse, the balance in the Warehouse Account will increase. Similarly, when items are delivered from the Warehouse, an expense will be booked, and the balance in the Warehouse Account will reduce.

1. How to activate perpetual inventory 
Activate Perpetual Inventory:

Home > Accounting > Company > Enable Perpetual Inventory

Perpetual Inventory Note that if you disable perpetual inventory, users will have to manage the account entries manually.

Set up the following default accounts for each Company if not set. These accounts are created automatically in the new ERPNext accounts.

Default Inventory Account (Asset)
Stock Received But Not Billed (Liability)
Stock Adjustment Account (Expense)
Expenses Included In Valuation (Expense)
Cost Center
If the user wants to set an individual account for each warehouse, create account head for each account. Go to:

Accounts > Chart of Accounts > Company > Application of Funds (Assets) > Current Asset > Stock Assets > Create a new account with same name as Warehouse

Now, go to a warehouse and link this account to the warehouse. This helps in filtering and viewing statements warehouse-wise.

For stock transactions, general ledger entries made against the Account Head set on the warehouse, if the user had not set the account for the warehouse then the system gets the account head from the parent warehouse. If Account was not set for parent warehouse then the system gets the account(Default Inventory Account) from the company master.

An Item Group is a way to classify items based on types.

Depending on the type of product, you can categorize an item under its respective field. If the product is service-oriented, assign it under the Item Group - service. If the product is used as a raw-material, assign it under the Raw Material category. In case, an item is used only in trading, you can categorize it under an Item Group called Trading.

To access the Item Group list, go to:

Home > Stock > Items and Pricing > Item Group

This is what the Item Group tree looks like: 

1. How to create an Item Group 
Go to the Item Group list, click on New.

Select a group node under which you wish to create the Item Group, the default root is 'All Item Groups'.

Select 'Add Child' or click on the New button.

To make this child a category/group node, tick on Group Node.

Click on Create New.

Note:

Nodes in different parts of the tree cannot have the same name.

The child notes get alphabetically arranged.



1.2 Delete an Item Group 
Select the Item Group you want to delete.

Select 'Delete'.

Click on Yes.

2. Features 
To see the following options, click on an Item Group, click on Edit.

2.1 Parent Item Group 
You can change the parent Item Group of an item by choosing another one under General Settings.

2.2 Defaults 
Default Price List: A default price list that'll determine the Item Prices for this Item Group.

Default Warehouse: Default Warehouse set in transactions for the items that belong to this group.

Default Buying/Selling Cost Center: The default Buying/Selling Cost Center to which items in this group will be billed against.

Default Expense/Income Account: The default accounts for items that belong to this group.

Default Supplier: On setting a Supplier here, this supplier will be chosen in purchase transactions by default for items in this group.

2.3 Item Tax 
A default item tax template will be applied to all items belonging to this group. Similarly a Tax Category can also be selected, visit Quotation to know more about Tax Categories.

2.4 Website Settings 
Show in Website: Items belonging to this group will be shown on your website under the Item Group.

Weightage: This is the weight for the Item Groups themselves, item groups with higher weights will be shown first.

Slideshow: A slideshow for the Item Group, just like in an Item. Visit the Homepage page in Website module to know more.

Description: This will appear on the Item Group page.

Website Specifications: Label and its description for an item group.

Stock Reconciliation is the process of counting and evaluating material/products, periodically at the year end.

This is done in order to:

Keep the actual physical stock count and book stock count in sync

Value the stock for preparation of the accounting statements

The Stock Reconciliation feature in ERPNext is used for:

Posting opening stock

Reconciling book and actual stock

To access the Stock Reconciliation list, go to: > Home > Stock > Tools > Stock Reconciliation

1. How to Create a Stock Reconciliation to Post Opening Stock 
Using stock reconciliation you can update the number of specific items in a warehouse as of specific time. You can also add Items in the stock which have Serial Numbers or the Batch Numbers.

Go to the Stock Reconciliation list, click on New.

Select the Purpose as 'Opening Stock'. You can edit the posting Date and Time.

Select Item Code, Warehouse, Quantity, and Valuation Rate. If there is a Serial / Batch No involved, add it.

If you want to auto-generate Serial No / Batch No then keep those fields blank.

For auto-generation of Serial No, you need to set "Serial Number Series" in the Item master.

For auto-generation of Batch no, you need to enable "Automatically Create New Batch" checkbox in the item master.

The Difference Account will be set as 'Temporary Opening'.

Save and Submit.



> Note: Maintain Stock option should be enabled in Item master for this to work.

2. How to Create a Stock Reconciliation to Reconcile Book and Physical Stock Count 
Stock Reconciliation is the process of counting and evaluating stock-in-trade, periodically and at year-end in order to value the total stock for preparing accounting statements. In this process, the actual physical stocks are checked and recorded in the system. The actual stocks and the stock in the system should be in agreement and accurate. If they are not, you can use the Stock Reconciliation tool to reconcile stock balance and value with actuals.

To reconcile the stock:

Go to the Stock Reconciliation list, click on New

Select the Purpose as 'Stock Reconciliation'. You can edit the posting Date and Time.

Set Item Code, Warehouse.

The current Quantity and Valuation Rate will be fetched, change the quantity as required.

The expense account in Difference Account will be set to 'Stock Adjustment' by default.

The Cost Center default will be 'Main', change if needed.

Save and Submit.



3. Features 
3.1 Upload Data Through Spreadsheet 
If you have a lot of items, you can upload the details via a spreadsheet.

Download Template

Open new Stock Reconciliation and click on Download button to download the template in CSV format.



Enter Data in CSV Template.

The CSV format is case-sensitive. Do not edit the headers which are pre-set in the template. In the Item Code and Warehouse column, enter exact Item Code and Warehouse as created in your ERPNext account. For quantity, enter the stock level you wish to set for that item, in a specific warehouse.



Upload the CSV file with the data by clicking on 'Upload' button.



Review, Save and Submit.



Check Stock Ledger Report for updated stock balance.



3.2 Get Stock Balance and Valuation as of Specific Date and Time 
You can import the stock balance and valuation as of specific date and time from a selected Warehouse by clicking on Items button. You can update the Quantity and Valuation Rate as needed.



3.3 Using barcode scanner to scan physical inventory 
If you have configured barcodes for your items you can use a barcode scanner to reconcile physical quantities. To do this follow these steps:

Set default warehouse

Enable "Scan Mode" this will disable fetching existing quantity and let you add quantities by incrementally scanning items.

Click on "Scan Barcode" field and use your barcode scanner to send input. Reconciliation items table will will keep getting updated as you scan items. Following video demonstrates this process.



4. How Stock Reconciliation Works 
Once a stock reconciliation is posted to update the quantity on specific date and time for an item in a warehouse, it will not be modified by subsequent stock transactions even if such transactions have a posting date which is prior to the stock reconciliation date. In other words, backdated entries will not change the stock numbers after a Stock Reconciliation entry is posted.

Examples are as follows.

Before reconciliation, the valuation rate was 530 and the available qty was 6, so the total stock value was 3,180. After reconciliation, the valuation rate has changed to 620 and available qty changed to 3, so the new stock value becomes 1,860. To adjust the stock value in the accounting, the system has credited extra amount 3,180 - 1,860 = 1,320 to Warehouse's account and debited to stock adjustment account. The GL entries for the above entry is as follows: To view GL entries, click on button View > Accounting Ledger  The stock balance after submission of the stock reconciliation:  The general ledger for the warehouse account Nagpur after submission of the stock reconciliation:  ### 4.3 For Batch Items Stock reconciliation for batch items will be used to add a new batch or to update the quantity of the existing batch. 5. Serial and Batch Bundle 
In version 15 the serial and batch bundle feature has introduced to make stock transaction against the serial no / batch items. For stock reconciliation, user gets two option to make serial and batch bundle.

Use Serial / Batch Fields:

The user can use the old serial / batch fields to make serial and batch bundle automatically. In this case user has to enable the checkbox "
Use Serial No / Batch Fields" in the line item



Use Serial / Batch Bundle:

The user can use the Serial / Batch bundle to make stock reconciliation for serialized / batched items. Here user gets option to either "Reconcile All Serial Nos / Batches" or "Reconcile Selected Serial Nos / Batches"

Reconcile Selected Serial Nos / Batches: The user needs to disable the "Reconcile All Serial Nos / Batches" checkbox and create a serial and batch bundle for specific serial numbers or batches. By doing this, the system will automatically create the Current Serial / Batch Bundle for the serial numbers or batches which has been selected by the user manually within the Serial and Batch Bundle.



For example, if the user has 10 batches and wants to change the valuation rate of only 2 batches, then the user should disable the "Reconcile All Serial Nos / Batches" checkbox, and create the serial and batch bundle for those 2 batches with the new valuation rate.

Reconcile All Serial Nos / Batches: The user needs to enable the checkbox "Reconcile All Serial Nos / Batches" and create a serial and batch bundle.



For example, if the user has 10 batches and wants to reconcile and keep only one batch. Using the stock reconciliation, the user will be able to consume 9 batches automatically and retain one batch. For that, the user has to enable the "Reconcile All Serial Nos / Batches" checkbox in the Stock Reconciliation Item, and then the system will automatically consume 9 batches and add one batch on submission of the stock reconciliation.

-- Constants for controlling plane steering behavior
local PITCH_UP_THRESHOLD	= -15		-- Pitch angle threshold in degrees

local YAW_FACTOR			= 1			-- Multiplicative factor for yaw adjustment

    LEFT		= vec3(-1, 0, 0),
    UP			= vec3(0, 0, 1),
    DOWN		= vec3(0, 0, -1)

-- Calculate the signed angle between two vectors with respect to a reference axis
local function calculateSignedAngle(from, to, axis)
    local fromNormalized, toNormalized = from:clone():normalize(), to:clone():normalize()
    local dotProduct = fromNormalized:dot(toNormalized)
    local angle = math.acos(math.max(-1, math.min(1, dotProduct)))    -- Clamp the dot product
    local crossProduct = fromNormalized:cross(toNormalized)
    local sign = crossProduct:dot(axis) < 0 and -1 or 1
    return angle * sign
end

-- Calculate the angle between two vectors in degrees
local function calculateAngleBetweenVectors(v1, v2)
    local normV1, normV2 = v1:normalize(), v2:normalize()
    local dotProduct = math.max(-1, math.min(1, normV1:dot(normV2)))    -- Clamp the dot product
    return math.deg(math.acos(dotProduct))
end

-- Obtain the conjugate of a quaternion
local function conjugateQuaternion(q)
    return quat(-q.x, -q.y, -q.z, q.w)
end

-- Smooth step function
local function smoothstep(edge0, edge1, x)
    x = math.max(0, math.min(1, (x - edge0) / (edge1 - edge0)))
    return x * x * (3 - 2 * x)
end

-- Compute the steering input for the plane to move towards a target position
local function computeSteeringInput(plane, dt, targetPosition)
    local planePosition = vec3(getCarCoordinates(plane))
    local planeRotation = quat(getVehicleQuaternion(plane))

    local positionError = targetPosition - planePosition
    local distanceError = positionError:length()
    local localError = conjugateQuaternion(planeRotation) * positionError

    local errorDir = localError:normalize()
    local pitchError, rollError, yawError
    pitchError = vec3(0, localError.y, localError.z):normalize()
    rollError = vec3(localError.x, localError.y, 0):normalize()
    yawError = vec3(localError.x, 0, localError.z):normalize()

    local targetInput = vec3()
    local pitch = calculateSignedAngle(DIRECTION.FORWARD, pitchError, DIRECTION.RIGHT)

    if -pitch < PITCH_UP_THRESHOLD then
        pitch = (pitch + 360) % 360
    end
    targetInput.x = pitch

    local angleError = calculateAngleBetweenVectors(DIRECTION.FORWARD, rollError)
    local minAngle, maxAngle = -5, FINE_STEERING_ANGLE

    local angleError = calculateAngleBetweenVectors(DIRECTION.FORWARD, rollError)
    local dynamicYawFactor = smoothstep(minAngle, maxAngle, angleError) * YAW_FACTOR

    if angleError < FINE_STEERING_ANGLE then
        local yaw = -calculateSignedAngle(DIRECTION.FORWARD, yawError, DIRECTION.UP)
        targetInput.y = yaw * dynamicYawFactor
    else
        local roll = calculateSignedAngle(DIRECTION.UP, rollError, DIRECTION.FORWARD)
        targetInput.z = roll * ROLL_FACTOR
    end

    local function clampInput(value)
        return math.max(-1, math.min(1, value))
    end

    targetInput.x, targetInput.y, targetInput.z = clampInput(targetInput.x), clampInput(targetInput.y), clampInput(targetInput.z)

    local input = vec3()
    input.x = clampInput(input.x + (targetInput.x - input.x) * STEERING_SPEED * dt)
    input.y = clampInput(input.y + (targetInput.y - input.y) * STEERING_SPEED * dt)
    input.z = clampInput(input.z + (targetInput.z - input.z) * STEERING_SPEED * dt)

    return targetInput
end

function dxDrawRing(posX, posY, radius, width, startAngle, amount, color, absoluteAmount, anglesPerLine)
    if type(posX) ~= "number" or type(posY) ~= "number" or type(startAngle) ~= "number" or type(amount) ~= "number" then
        print("Error: One of the required parameters (posX, posY, startAngle, amount) is not a number.")
        return false
    end

    radius = type(radius) == "number" and radius or 50
    width = type(width) == "number" and width or 5
    color = color or 0xFFFFFFFF
    absoluteAmount = type(absoluteAmount) == "boolean" and absoluteAmount or false
    anglesPerLine = type(anglesPerLine) == "number" and anglesPerLine or 1

    local stopAngle = absoluteAmount and (amount + startAngle) or ((amount * 360) + startAngle)

    for angle = startAngle, stopAngle, anglesPerLine do
        local radAngle = math.rad(angle)
        local startX = math.cos(radAngle) * (radius - width)
        local startY = math.sin(radAngle) * (radius - width)
        local endX = math.cos(radAngle) * (radius + width)
        local endY = math.sin(radAngle) * (radius + width)

        renderDrawLine(startX + posX, startY + posY, endX + posX, endY + posY, width, color)
    end

    return math.floor((stopAngle - startAngle) / anglesPerLine)
end

Which of the ISO/IEC 2700X standards (as well as their clauses and subclauses) reflect the requirements related to the information security risk management process. For example, in the context of information security of a banking organization?


The ISO/IEC 27000 series of standards is specifically designed to help organizations manage their information security processes. The series is extensive, but the standards most pertinent to information security risk management are ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 27005. Here's how they break down:

ISO/IEC 27001: Information Security Management Systems (ISMS) - Requirements
ISO/IEC 27001 is the central standard for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and improving an Information Security Management System. It contains explicit requirements for risk management in the context of information security:

Clause 4: Context of the Organization
Understand the organization and its context.
Understanding the needs and expectations of interested parties.
Determining the scope of the ISMS.
ISMS and its processes.
Clause 6: Planning
6.1 Actions to address risks and opportunities
6.1.1 General – requires planning to manage risks.
6.1.2 Information security risk assessment – involves identifying and assessing information security risks.
6.1.3 Information security risk treatment – involves selecting risk treatment options.
6.2 Information Security Objectives and Planning to Achieve Them
Clause 8: Operation
8.2 Information security risk assessment
8.3 Information security risk treatment
ISO/IEC 27005: Information Security Risk Management
ISO/IEC 27005 provides guidance on risk management in the context of information security, offering a more detailed look at risk management beyond the requirements listed in ISO/IEC 27001:

Clause 7: Information Security Risk Management Process
7.1 Context Establishment
Understanding the organization's environment and boundaries for risk management.
7.2 Risk Assessment
Risk identification
Risk analysis
Risk evaluation
7.3 Risk Treatment
Selecting and implementing measures.
7.4 Risk Acceptance
Acceptance criteria and decision-making.
7.5 Risk Communication
7.6 Risk Monitoring and Review
Ensuring that risks and their treatments are actively managed.
Clauses 9 and 10:
Provide additional guidance on maintaining and adapting the risk management process.
ISO/IEC 27002: Code of Practice for Information Security Controls
While ISO/IEC 27002 does not specify risk management processes, it supports ISO/IEC 27001 with guidelines and best practices for implementing specific controls. This can be beneficial in risk treatment selection when aligning with ISO/IEC 27001's requirements.

Implementation in a Banking Context
For a banking organization, particularly sensitive and regulated, integrating these standards involves developing a detailed ISMS tailored to their unique environment. This involves aligning the risk management process with regulatory requirements from entities like the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and ensuring that specific banking risks are appropriately addressed.

Overall, the combination of ISO/IEC 27001's high-level framework requirements and ISO/IEC 27005's deeper dive into the risk management process provides a robust foundation for securing banking information systems against risks.

I am preparing for an intense DBMS (Database Management Systems) interview, and I need a highly comprehensive, detailed, and in-depth set of notes that covers everything about DBMS from the ground up. I want this material to be so thorough that I can confidently answer any question an interviewer might ask, regardless of its complexity or obscurity.

The notes should leave absolutely nothing out, covering DBMS theory, architecture, practical applications, and implementation strategies. I need detailed explanations of each topic, accompanied by real-world examples, diagrams, and comparisons to make the concepts clear and digestible.

The following topics should be included, but not limited to:

1. Introduction to DBMS
What is a DBMS? Why do we use it?
The difference between file systems and DBMS.
Advantages of DBMS over traditional file systems.
Real-world examples where DBMS is essential.
2. Database Models and Schemas
Detailed breakdown of ER models, relational models, network models, hierarchical models, object-oriented models.
Schema architecture (Physical, Logical, View).
Entity-Relationship (ER) Diagrams: Detailed explanation, including entities, attributes, and relationships.
Mapping ER diagrams to relational models.
3. Database Normalization
Deep dive into normalization: Explain First Normal Form (1NF) to Fifth Normal Form (5NF).
Functional dependencies and their role in normalization.
Denormalization: When and why we denormalize.
4. SQL (Structured Query Language)
Cover every aspect of SQL: DDL (CREATE, ALTER, DROP), DML (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE), DCL (GRANT, REVOKE), and TCL (COMMIT, ROLLBACK).
Detailed breakdown of complex queries, subqueries, joins (inner, outer, left, right), unions, intersections, and set operations.
Query optimization: Explain indexes, query plans, and how databases execute queries behind the scenes.
5. Relational Algebra and Relational Calculus
Detailed explanation of relational algebra: Selection, projection, union, set difference, Cartesian product, joins.
Relational calculus: Tuple and domain relational calculus, including their importance in query languages.
6. Transactions and Concurrency Control
Transactions: Definition, properties (ACID), and examples.
Concurrency Control: Why it's necessary, methods like two-phase locking (2PL), timestamp ordering, and multiversion concurrency control (MVCC).
Isolation levels: Read uncommitted, read committed, repeatable read, and serializable—what they mean and where they apply.
Deadlock: How it occurs and how to prevent or resolve it.
7. Database Storage and File Organization
Explain the types of file organization: Heap files, sorted files, and hashing.
Indexing: Single-level, multi-level, clustered, and non-clustered indexing.
B-trees and B+ trees: How they work, why they're used in DBMS, and their role in indexing.
Hashing: Static and dynamic hashing, extendible hashing, and linear hashing.
8. Query Processing and Optimization
Explain query processing stages: Parsing, optimization, execution.
Query optimization techniques: Cost-based vs. rule-based optimization, the role of indexes, join algorithms (nested-loop join, hash join, sort-merge join).
Execution plans: How they are generated, what they represent, and how to analyze and improve them.
9. Transaction Management and Recovery
ACID properties revisited, focusing on practical applications.
Concurrency anomalies: Lost updates, dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, and phantom reads.
Recovery mechanisms: Write-ahead logging, checkpoints, shadow paging, undo/redo operations.
Crash recovery in distributed systems.
10. Distributed Databases
What distributed databases are and why they are used.
Challenges in distributed databases: Network partitioning, replication, consistency, and latency.
CAP Theorem: Detailed explanation and implications for database systems.
Distributed transactions: Two-phase commit, three-phase commit.
Concepts of sharding, partitioning, and replication.
11. NoSQL Databases
NoSQL: What it is, why it's important, and the different types (document stores, key-value stores, column stores, graph databases).
Detailed comparison between NoSQL and traditional relational databases.
Use cases where NoSQL is better suited than SQL.
Eventual consistency vs. strong consistency in NoSQL systems.
Popular NoSQL databases: MongoDB, Cassandra, Redis, etc.
12. Big Data and Database Integration
How DBMS fits into the world of Big Data.
Hadoop and DBMS integration: How DBMS can be used with Hadoop for efficient data management.
In-memory databases: What they are and when to use them.
Sharding, replication, and partitioning in large-scale data systems.
NewSQL: What it is, its advantages over traditional SQL and NoSQL systems.
13. Database Security
Explain authentication and authorization methods in DBMS.
Encryption: Both at-rest and in-transit encryption mechanisms.
SQL Injection: How it works, prevention techniques.
Auditing and logging: Why they are essential for security and compliance.
14. Backup and Recovery Techniques
Backup types: Full, incremental, differential, and mirror backups.
Backup strategies for large-scale databases.
Disaster recovery: Techniques and tools.
How to design a reliable and secure backup plan.
15. Database Tuning and Performance Optimization
Query tuning: Explain how to optimize complex queries.
Index tuning: How to choose the right indexes, how to monitor index performance.
Caching mechanisms: The role of caching in DBMS performance.
Database configuration settings that affect performance.
16. Emerging Trends in DBMS
Cloud databases: AWS RDS, Google Cloud SQL, Azure SQL, and their key features.
AI and ML in databases: How machine learning and AI are being integrated with DBMS.
Blockchain databases: What they are, how they work, and why they are becoming relevant.
Edge computing and DBMS: How databases are being optimized for edge devices.
17. Database Design Best Practices
Best practices for designing scalable, maintainable, and secure databases.
Trade-offs between normalization and denormalization for performance.
Common design pitfalls and how to avoid them.
18. Practical Application of DBMS in Real-world Systems
Case studies of database implementations in industries like e-commerce, healthcare, banking, and social media.
Real-world problems and how DBMS solves them.

Legal Guidelines
Like any online service, the Matrix.org Foundation receives requests for information about users. Those requests come from government agencies, law enforcement, individuals, and companies. We aim to be transparent about the data we collect about our users, through our privacy notice. This document describes the steps we take when engaging with law enforcement, and how we safeguard privacy rights. We also set out how law enforcement can send us requests.

Before revealing any non-public information about a site, an account, or a user, we require a valid subpoena, search warrant, or court order. The only exception is when we have a good faith belief that there is an emergency involving imminent danger of death or serious physical injury.

Law Enforcement Requests
To make a request, you will need a warrant issued by a UK authority in compliance with the UK Investigatory Powers Act of 2016 (“the Act”). We respond to requests from the United Kingdom only, in the form of authorisations which comply with article 66 of the aforementioned Act. Law enforcement agencies from outside the UK may obtain these types of authorisations through the Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty (MLAT).

These requests must be sent to <PRESIDIO_ANONYMIZED_EMAIL_ADDRESS>, and should include the following:

Details of the authorising officer, as per 61 (1) of the Act;
Details of the purpose for the request, as per 61 (7) of the Act.
We will only transfer information using end to end encryption.

Emergency Requests from Government Agencies/Law Enforcement
We may disclose user information to government or law enforcement agencies – without a warrant – if we have a good faith belief that an emergency involving** imminent danger of death or serious physical injury** requires disclosure of information related to the emergency without delay.

Send your emergency request to <PRESIDIO_ANONYMIZED_EMAIL_ADDRESS> and include “emergency” in the subject line.

Include all information you have about the situation so that we may evaluate the urgency of your request, making sure that you indicate if the request is confidential.
Include the details of your agency, and your contact details.
If you make no mention of confidentiality, we will notify the user(s) affected.
What Information Do We Have?
The data available on Matrix.org users is limited to that which is described in our privacy notice. As per the Matrix protocol, homeserver administrators are unable to view data which is end-to-end encrypted, making this type of data out of scope for these requests.

We do not voluntarily provide governments with access to data about users for any reason, including for the purposes of law enforcement, intelligence gathering, or other surveillance. As noted above, we only provide information to third parties after receiving a valid search warrant.

Notification to Matrix.org Users
We aim for total transparency with our users when legal requests for information or complaints affect their account. It is our policy to notify users and provide them with a copy of any legal requests regarding their account or site, unless we are prohibited from doing so by the warrant. When the prohibition from notifying users expires, we will notify users and provide them with a copy of the legal request at that time.

Preservation Requests by Government and Law Enforcement Agencies
It is our policy to notify users and provide them with a copy of any legal requests regarding their account, unless we are prohibited from doing so by a valid warrant issued in the UK, as described in the sections below. Our policy of notifying users about requests to preserve their information is meant to protect user privacy and promote transparency, while also avoiding interference with legitimate investigations of criminal activity.

Preservation requests may only be submitted by government and law enforcement agencies conducting a criminal investigation in which the information sought is relevant. We will preserve records for 90 days in response to a valid request, which the government or law enforcement agency can extend upon request.

We will act upon requests from non-UK law enforcement agencies only when these originate via the Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty process (MLAT).

Send your preservation requests to <PRESIDIO_ANONYMIZED_EMAIL_ADDRESS>.

Other types of requests
Reporting Terms of Service Violations
If you believe that a user or room is violating our Terms and Conditions, please report this information via <PRESIDIO_ANONYMIZED_EMAIL_ADDRESS> providing as much information as possible, and we will take action as appropriate.

We do not remove content based on disagreements, allegations or breaches of rules related to specific communities. Removal of content will only occur when it breaches our Terms. We may refer information about accounts sharing illegal content to the relevant authorities.

Requests for Takedown of Copyrighted Content
Matrix.org complies with properly formatted notices sent in accordance with the Digital Millennium Copyright Act. More information about our process and a DMCA takedown notice submission form can be found here.

Our stances
Who Is Liable for Content Hosted on Matrix.org?
We do not control or endorse the materials or message content found in any rooms or communities. To the maximum extent permitted by law, Matrix.org will have no liability related to user materials arising under intellectual property rights, libel, privacy, publicity, obscenity or other laws. Matrix.org also disclaims all liability with respect to the misuse, loss, modification or unavailability of any user messages or files.

On Back Doors and Encryption
We are strong advocates for encryption as a tool to support everyone’s human right to privacy. Matrix.org will never support encryption backdoors and will only share information which is requested following the above guidelines.

For more information on our approach to encryption and abuse management, please read through this blog post.»

Here are the strategies: # Stock Selection Strategies for Quick Growth

## Strategy 1: Sentiment-Momentum Hybrid

This strategy combines sentiment analysis with price momentum to identify stocks that are both positively perceived and showing strong recent performance.

### Inputs:
1. Number of articles analyzed
2. Average sentiment score
3. Recent price performance (e.g., 1-month and 3-month returns)
4. Trading volume

### Methodology:
1. Filter stocks with a minimum of 10 articles analyzed to ensure sufficient coverage.
2. Rank stocks by their average sentiment score, focusing on those with scores above 0.5 (on a scale from -1 to 1).
3. Calculate the 1-month and 3-month price returns for each stock.
4. Rank stocks based on their price momentum (average of 1-month and 3-month returns).
5. Calculate the average daily trading volume over the past month and rank stocks based on liquidity.
6. Combine the sentiment, momentum, and volume rankings with equal weighting.
7. Select the top 5-10 stocks with the highest combined ranking.

### Rationale:
This strategy aims to capture stocks that are not only viewed positively by the market but are also demonstrating strong price action and sufficient liquidity. The combination of sentiment and momentum can help identify stocks with potential for continued growth.

## Strategy 2: Sentiment-Value-Growth Blend

This approach combines sentiment analysis with fundamental value and growth metrics to find stocks that are undervalued but have strong growth potential and positive market perception.

### Inputs:
1. Number of articles analyzed
2. Average sentiment score
3. Price-to-Earnings (P/E) ratio
4. Price-to-Book (P/B) ratio
5. Earnings growth rate (past 3 years)
6. Revenue growth rate (past 3 years)

### Methodology:
1. Filter stocks with a minimum of 15 articles analyzed for robust sentiment data.
2. Rank stocks by their average sentiment score, focusing on those with scores above 0.3.
3. Calculate a value score based on P/E and P/B ratios (lower is better).
4. Calculate a growth score based on earnings and revenue growth rates (higher is better).
5. Normalize all scores to a 0-100 scale.
6. Combine the sentiment (40%), value (30%), and growth (30%) scores.
7. Select the top 5-10 stocks with the highest combined scores.

### Rationale:
This strategy aims to identify stocks that are positively perceived by the market, have attractive valuations, and demonstrate strong historical growth. The combination of these factors can potentially lead to stocks with significant upside potential.

## Strategy 3: Sentiment-Driven Sector Rotation

This strategy uses sentiment analysis to identify the most promising sectors, then selects the best-performing stocks within those sectors.

### Inputs:
1. Number of articles analyzed (per stock and aggregated by sector)
2. Average sentiment score (per stock and aggregated by sector)
3. Sector performance (1-month and 3-month returns)
4. Individual stock performance within sectors
5. Relative Strength Index (RSI) for stocks

### Methodology:
1. Aggregate sentiment scores and article counts for each sector.
2. Rank sectors based on their average sentiment scores and recent performance.
3. Select the top 2-3 sectors with the highest combined sentiment and performance scores.
4. Within each selected sector:
   a. Filter stocks with a minimum of 10 articles analyzed.
   b. Rank stocks by their individual sentiment scores.
   c. Calculate a performance score based on 1-month and 3-month returns.
   d. Use RSI to identify stocks that are not overbought (RSI < 70).
   e. Combine sentiment, performance, and RSI rankings.
5. Select the top 2-3 stocks from each chosen sector based on the combined rankings.

### Rationale:
This strategy leverages sector rotation principles, focusing on sectors with positive sentiment and strong recent performance. By then selecting the best stocks within these sectors, it aims to capitalize on both broad market trends and individual stock strength.

## Implementation Considerations:

1. Regularly update and backtest these strategies to ensure their effectiveness in current market conditions.
2. Consider implementing risk management techniques, such as position sizing and stop-loss orders.
3. Monitor the selected stocks closely and be prepared to adjust positions based on changes in sentiment or other key metrics.
4. Combine these strategies with thorough fundamental analysis and due diligence before making investment decisions.

3. **Craft an Engaging First Line**: The first line of your summary is crucial. It should grab the reader's attention and make them want to read more. Use a short, punchy statement that resonates with the audience.

4. **Cover the Main Topics and Guests**: Summarize the main topics discussed in the episode. If there were any guests, mention their names and what they contributed to the conversation.

5. **Include Teaser Information**: Provide enough information to pique the reader's interest without giving away too much. Teasers can include interesting facts, quotes, or insights from the episode.

6. **Optimize for SEO**: Use relevant keywords in your summary to improve its visibility in search engine results. This helps potential listeners find your podcast more easily.

7. **Keep It Concise**: Aim for a summary that is between one and two paragraphs long. Be clear and concise, focusing on the most important points.

8. **Use Bullet Points**: Organize information using bullet points to make it easy to read at a glance. This is especially useful for episodes that cover multiple topics.

9. **Make It Engaging**: Use language that is exciting and fun to read. Choose words that catch the reader's attention and spark their curiosity.

10. **Review and Edit**: Once you've written your summary, review it for clarity, accuracy, and engagement. Make sure it accurately represents the episode and is free of errors.

can you improve this pricing model to make it great value for the customer but also as profitable as possible for the company: Your pricing model for a Voice AI agent tailored to real estate brokerages sounds solid, and I like the idea of a tiered approach for scaling. Here are some suggestions to fine-tune it and make sure it’s attractive, scalable, and profitable:

1. Base Retainer Fee:

	•	$500/month per agent is a reasonable starting point for a smaller brokerage that wants to test out the system. This fee should cover basic access to your AI agent and support.
	•	Be sure to communicate the key value (e.g., cost savings on staffing, 24/7 availability, instant follow-up, lead qualification, etc.) to justify this price.

2. Volume Discounting (For Scaling):

As you mentioned, the price per agent should decrease significantly as the brokerage scales up its use of your AI agents. Here’s a possible breakdown:

	•	$500 per agent/month for 1-10 agents.
	•	$350 per agent/month for 11-100 agents.
	•	$150 per agent/month for 101-999 agents.
	•	$75 per agent/month for 1,000+ agents.

You can adjust these thresholds based on client size, but this tiered pricing gives larger brokerages incentive to adopt your service at scale.

3. Pay-per-Minute/Message Charges:

Similar to Twilio’s model, you can charge for the usage of the agents by adding call and messaging costs on top of the monthly retainer. This could be:

	•	Voice calls: $0.03 - $0.05 per minute.
	•	SMS/Messaging: $0.01 - $0.02 per message.

This aligns with the fact that AI agents will consume resources like Twilio APIs for calls and messaging, and these charges ensure you’re covering that cost.

4. Onboarding/Setup Fee:

	•	Optionally, you could charge an initial setup fee for configuring the Voice AI agent for the client’s CRM and systems. This could be around $1000-$2000, depending on the complexity of the setup and integrations.
	•	You could waive or reduce this fee for larger clients (e.g., those committing to 50+ agents), making it more attractive for them to scale with you.

5. Support Fees:

	•	Basic Support could be included in the monthly fee.
	•	Premium Support (e.g., dedicated account manager, faster response times, advanced analytics) could be an optional add-on for larger clients, priced at $100-$300/month depending on their size.

6. Long-Term Commitment Discounts:

	•	Offer a discount for clients committing to 6 or 12 months in advance, e.g., a 10-20% discount for longer commitments.
	•	This incentivizes clients to lock in, stabilizing your cash flow.

7. Performance-Based Upsell:

	•	You could also build in performance-based upselling, where if the AI agent is performing exceptionally (e.g., exceeding a certain number of booked appointments or qualified leads), you could offer them additional services or a higher-tier plan with added features (e.g., advanced analytics, CRM automation, etc.).

8. Usage-Based Scaling:

In addition to charging by the number of agents, you might also consider usage-based pricing if the volume of calls/messages varies significantly among clients. For example:

	•	Start with a basic package of X minutes and Y messages per month.
	•	Additional usage (above the included minutes/messages) can be charged at a per-minute or per-message rate, as mentioned above.

Example Model:

For a smaller brokerage (1-10 agents):

	•	Base fee: $500/agent/month.
	•	Usage fee: $0.03/minute for calls, $0.02 per message.
	•	Setup fee: $1000 (waived for 12-month commitment).

For a large brokerage (1,000+ agents):

	•	Base fee: $75/agent/month.
	•	Usage fee: $0.03/minute for calls, $0.02 per message.
	•	Setup fee: Waived for high-volume clients.

This structure provides clear value at every scale, helps you cover costs, and incentivizes clients to increase their usage.

and Zeng Fanzhi’s Mask Series No. 11 (fig. 3), offer a commonality in their
thematic and expressive exploration of the human condition in modern
urban centres. This study aims to explore the notion of alienation as a
product of the urban environment, and humans as subjects to their
surroundings. These works have been selected under the thematic and
conceptual framework of urban alienation and thus will be analysed in
close relation to this theme.
The response will first focus on the emotional reality and narrative fiction
presented in Edward Hopper’s Automat, and will be analysed as a portrait
of loneliness, presenting a figure detached from their world and absorbed
in themselves.
Contrasting greatly in media, George Segal instead explores the theme
through sculpture, and illustrates human subjects in familiar and immediate
environments, depicted in tableaux of apathy.
Zeng Fanzhi’s Mask Series comments on isolation through the
employment of significant symbols, and Mask Series No. 11 specifically,
which will be analysed thirdly, serves as a valid portrayal of the difficulties
of rapid urbanisation experienced in 20th century China, in addition to
presenting urban alienation in a markedly different cultural context.
In analysing and comparing the formal qualities, the sociocultural context
and conceptual significance of the artworks, this study aims to provide a
cohesive understanding on how these three artists depict human subjects
in isolation. Additionally, I hope to demonstrate the influence of stated
artworks in concept, material and understanding of formal qualities in my
own art-making."

    def _add_scrollable_canvas(self, sidebar: tk.Frame):
        """Add scrollable canvas for table labels."""
        scrollbar_frame = self._create_frame(
            parent=sidebar,
            width=self.sidebar_width,
            bg=self.sidebar_color
        )
        scrollbar_frame.grid(row=1, column=0, sticky='nsew', padx=10, pady=10)
        scrollbar_frame.columnconfigure(0, weight=1)
        scrollbar_frame.rowconfigure(0, weight=1)

        canvas = tk.Canvas(
            scrollbar_frame,
            bg=self.sidebar_color,
            highlightthickness=0
        )
        canvas.grid(row=0, column=0, sticky='nsew')

        self.config_scrollbar_style()

        scrollbar = ttk.Scrollbar(
            scrollbar_frame,
            orient="vertical",
            command=canvas.yview,
            style="Custom.Vertical.TScrollbar"
        )
        scrollbar.grid(row=0, column=1, sticky='ns')

        canvas.configure(yscrollcommand=scrollbar.set)

        self.table_labels_frame = tk.Frame(canvas, bg=self.sidebar_color)
        canvas.create_window((0, 0), window=self.table_labels_frame, anchor="nw")

        canvas.bind("<MouseWheel>", lambda event: canvas.yview_scroll(int(-1 * (event.delta / 120)), "units"))

        self.table_labels_frame.bind("<Configure>", lambda event: canvas.configure(scrollregion=canvas.bbox("all")))
        scrollbar_frame.bind("<Configure>", lambda event: self._update_scrollbar(scrollbar_frame, canvas, scrollbar))

    def _update_scrollbar(self, scrollbar_frame, canvas, scrollbar):
        """Update scrollbar visibility based on content size."""
        canvas.update_idletasks()
        canvas_height = scrollbar_frame.winfo_height()
        content_height = self.table_labels_frame.winfo_reqheight()

        if content_height > canvas_height:
            scrollbar.grid()
            canvas.configure(yscrollcommand=scrollbar.set)
            canvas.bind("<MouseWheel>", lambda event: canvas.yview_scroll(int(-1 * (event.delta / 120)), "units"))
        else:
            scrollbar.grid_remove()
            canvas.configure(yscrollcommand=lambda *args: None)
            canvas.unbind("<MouseWheel>")

    def _create_clickable_label(
        self,
        parent: tk.Widget,
        text: str,
        command,
        allow_rename: bool = False,
        anchor: str = 'w'
    ) -> tk.Label:
        """Create a clickable label with optional rename functionality."""
        cursor = "arrow" if allow_rename else "hand2"
        label = tk.Label(
            parent,
            text=text,
            bg=self.button_color,
            fg=self.text_color,
            cursor=cursor,
            anchor=anchor
        )
        label.bind("<Button-1>", lambda _: command())
        if allow_rename:
            label.bind("<Double-Button-1>", lambda _: self.begin_rename(text))
        return label

    def add_custom_hover(self, widget: tk.Widget):
        """Add custom hover effects to a widget."""
        widget.bind("<Enter>", lambda e: widget.config(bg=self.button_color_selected))
        widget.bind("<Leave>", lambda e: widget.config(bg=self.button_color))

User: What is the different beween junmai ginjo and jumai daiginjo sake?
Assistant: The primary difference between Junmai Ginjo and Junmai Daiginjo sake lies in the degree of rice polishing and the corresponding flavor profiles. Here’s a breakdown:

1. **Rice Polishing Ratio**:
   - **Junmai Ginjo**: The rice used in Junmai Ginjo sake must be polished to at least 60% of its original size, meaning 40% of the outer layer of each grain is milled away. This level of polishing generally results in a lighter, more fragrant sake with a complexity of flavors and aromas.
   - **Junmai Daiginjo**: This type of sake requires that the rice be polished to at least 50%, meaning at least half of the outer layer of each grain is milled away. Junmai Daiginjo is considered a more premium category than Junmai Ginjo and often exhibits an even more refined, delicate, and aromatic profile.

2. **Flavor and Aroma**:
   - **Junmai Ginjo**: Typically features a smooth, light texture with fruity and floral notes, sometimes accompanied by a subtle sweetness.
   - **Junmai Daiginjo**: Known for its elegant and complex flavor profile, it often has a more pronounced aroma with layers of fruit, floral notes, and a clean, refined finish.

3. **Price and Availability**:
   - **Junmai Daiginjo** sakes are generally more expensive due to the higher polishing requirement and often more labor-intensive production processes. As a result, they tend to be less commonly available than Junmai Ginjo.

Both styles of sake are brewed without the addition of distilled alcohol, as indicated by the “Junmai” prefix, meaning they rely solely on rice, water, yeast, and koji for their development. While both are premium sakes, the Daiginjo variant is usually considered the pinnacle of polished rice sakes, offering a more luxurious drinking experience.
User: how do you setup a debit order to pay off a credit card every month?
Assistant: Setting up a debit order to pay off your credit card each month is a convenient way to manage your payments and ensure that you don’t miss due dates. Here’s a step-by-step guide to setting one up:

1. **Check with Your Bank/Credit Card Issuer**:
   - Contact the bank or the institution that issued your credit card. This can typically be done through their customer service line, website, or mobile app.
   
2. **Gather Necessary Information**:
   - You will need your bank account details from which the debit order will be deducted. This usually includes the account number and the branch code or institution code.
   - Have your credit card details handy, such as the card number and potentially other identification information the issuer might require.

3. **Choose Payment Amount**:
   - Decide whether you want to pay the minimum amount due, the full statement balance, or a fixed amount each month.
   - Keep in mind that paying off the full balance every month is usually the best way to avoid interest charges.

4. **Set Up the Debit Order**:
   - Using the bank’s website or mobile app, you can often set up a debit order directly. Look for options related to bill payments or manage credit card accounts.
   - Alternatively, you may need to fill out a form either online or at the bank’s physical location. Some banks allow you to set this up over the phone.

5. **Specify Payment Date**:
   - Choose a date for the debit order. This date should be a few days before your credit card payment due date to ensure timely payment.
   - Make sure the date aligns with your cash flow, such as shortly after your payday.

6. **Confirm and Monitor**:
   - Confirm the setup of the debit order with your bank. They may provide you with a confirmation number or receipt.
   - Monitor your bank account and credit card statements to ensure the debit order is processed correctly. This is especially important for the first few months.

7. **Make Adjustments if Needed**:
   - If your financial situation changes, or if you decide to change the amount of your payments, contact your bank to adjust the debit order accordingly.

Setting up a debit order is a great way to automate your finances, but it's important to ensure that you have sufficient funds in your account when the debit occurs to avoid overdraft fees

We are committed to celebrating our culinary heritage while blending it with beloved global dishes, creating a unique fusion that delights taste buds everywhere. We strive to become a leading brand known for our creativity, quality, and the way we infuse Northeast Indian flavors into globally loved dishes. With every dish, we aim to showcase the best of our culinary traditions while continuously innovating and evolving.
Brand Story
Mo-Mogambo was born from a passion for food and a deep love for the flavors of Northeast India. The idea was simple: to take something beloved, like momos, and elevate it by fusing it with global dishes in a way that feels fresh and exciting. We wanted to create a brand that stands out, offering a unique twist on fast food while celebrating the rich culinary heritage of the Seven Sisters states.
The name "Mo-Mogambo" reflects this vision—it’s playful, memorable, and captures the bold spirit of our brand. By focusing on innovative flavors and personalized dishes, we’ve created a space where tradition meets modern trends, and food lovers can experience something truly special. From momos to fusion dishes like Mo-Noodles and Mo-Thukpa, we’re constantly evolving, always driven by creativity and a commitment to quality.
History
Mo-Mogambo started in Assam with a vision to bring the vibrant flavors of Northeast India to a wider audience. We knew we had something unique to offer—dishes that blend the authenticity of local spices with popular fast food favorites. After launching in Guwahati in 2023, the brand quickly became a local favorite, thanks to our creative menu and dedication to quality.
What makes Mo-Mogambo different is our ability to fuse tradition with innovation. We've taken familiar dishes and infused them with the flavors of the Northeast, creating a food experience that's both comforting and exciting. Our journey hasn’t always been smooth, but each challenge taught us resilience, and today, Mo-Mogambo stands as a beloved brand with ambitions to make a global mark.

The main goal of the most famous companies (as a rule, this is part of the mission statement) is aimed at creating benefits for a large number of people. The law of goal (mission) statements of successful world leaders: “The higher and nobler the company's goal, the more it encompasses people, companies, countries and industries, the more profitable the company will be...” N.d: Google: “to make the world's information universally accessible and useful”. 2. Ideal picture An ideal picture is an idea or statement about what the picture (area or product) should be. For example, the goal of a shoe store is obviously to sell shoes or provide people with shoes. The ideal picture is almost as simple: “This company sells shoes or provides shoes to people.” Now there is only one thing missing: the time factor. Then the complete ideal picture of a shoe store will be as follows: “The task of this enterprise is to provide people with shoes for ___ (time).” It can always exist, either for the life of the owner of this store, or for the time during which the owner of this store stays in this city, or for the duration of the fair. On my lonesome, I clacked away as the pitter patter of the rain colliding with the corrugated steel roofing shuddered. I’ve always had an interest in understanding things from the lowest levels, but it was this journey that really put into perspective how important resources are for learning. Purdue’s curriculum, which spans topics from embedded systems to artificial intelligence, is a perfect foundation for the broad technical expertise I hope to develop.
I’m particularly excited about Purdue’s research opportunities. Engaging in projects on Big Data and IoT would let me contribute to cutting-edge technology with the guidance of accomplished faculty. Through collaborative study tables and specialized coursework, Purdue is where I see myself translating my ideas into innovations that resonate far beyond just code.

I conducted a limited "covert reconnaissance" operation, meeting with a couple of QSs and a Symmal Project Manager from BTA to gather informal feedback on the challenges they encounter in their day-to-day tasks, especially concerning forecasting.
Here's a summary of the key issues they raised:
Month-End Timeline:
A recurring theme was the tight month-end timeline. BTA's monthly cycle begins on the 25th with the receipt of Payment Claims from subcontractors. Unlike the standard LOR timeline, which requires accruals by the 2nd of the following month, BTA requires them by the 28th of the same month. This leaves insufficient time for QSs and engineers to review and assess the claims, as many dockets received in the preceding days remain uncoded and are allocated to a "balancing account." This makes forecasting difficult and inaccurate, with costs scattered across various accounts.
The situation is compounded by the receipt of official CTD figures on the 4th of the month, followed by forecast reviews on the 7th. This limited timeframe prevents them from correcting misallocated costs, accurately assessing performance, and extrapolating data for the forecast.
Docket Management:
While they are satisfied with Virtual Superintendent (VS) for docket management, there's a significant lag between subcontractors starting on-site and being onboarded into the system. Even entered dockets are often miscoded due to the sheer number of cost codes, which supervisors haven't fully mastered. They estimate only 25% of dockets go through VS, forcing engineers to maintain their own spreadsheet trackers for accrual assessment. Symmal is particularly frustrated with this lack of visibility into costs and productivity.
Forecasting Process and Tools:
The current forecast spreadsheet (apparently inherited from John Holland) isn't integrated with PRISM or COINS, resulting in significant manual data entry. Engineers are expected to maintain traceability to Estimate line items, which often have different granularity than the delivery team's tracking requirements. The large number of cost codes further complicates the process, leading to misalignments between budget, actuals, and forecasts. The short turnaround time of 3-4 days for completing the forecast makes this period hectic and prone to errors. One engineer mentioned having at least $900,000 in costed but un-forecasted expenses simply because he couldn't determine their proper allocation.
COINS Structure:
Dividing the project into four separate COINS contracts creates duplication of effort and ambiguity regarding responsibilities for managing subcontract scopes. Cross-journaling costs and commitments between the four projects leads to frustration, as disconnected teams rely on each other to initiate journals, which isn't a seamless process. Change management is also complex, as budget owners have commitments against their codes from other projects due to urgent activities on the critical path, leaving insufficient time to award project-specific contracts.
Unassigned Budget Visibility:
The concept of assigned/unassigned budgets creates a disconnect between package managers and their "unassigned" scope, which cost planners forecast separately without considering factors beyond changed quantities. The teams believe this produces unrealistic forecasts, and they cannot reflect reality until the budget is "assigned" to them, forcing them to rebuild it from scratch.
